meta.title: Public Authority Assessment Dashboard
meta.note: Working sample of real organisations and their published codes. Nolan tags are two-layer: whether the code explicitly adopts the Seven Principles, and whether it substantively covers each principle. Every tag is evidenced from the source text.

principles.name: Selflessness
principles.def: Act solely in the public interest.

principles.name: Integrity
principles.def: Avoid obligations that could influence official duties.

principles.name: Objectivity
principles.def: Make choices on merit and evidence.

principles.name: Accountability
principles.def: Be accountable and submit to scrutiny.

principles.name: Openness
principles.def: Be as open as possible about decisions and actions.

principles.name: Leadership
principles.def: Promote and support these principles by example.

coc.note: Enumerates all seven Nolan principles with definitions, but as an appendix 'to remind Members' that 'do not form part of the Code of Conduct' (advisory, not binding clauses).

selflessness.evidence: Holders of public office should act solely in terms of the public interest.

integrity.evidence: Should not place themselves under any financial or other obligation to outside individuals or organisations that might seek to influence them.

accountability.evidence: Accountable for their decisions and actions to the public and must submit themselves to whatever scrutiny is appropriate.

openness.evidence: Should be as open as possible about all the decisions and actions that they take.

honesty.evidence: A duty to declare any private interests relating to their public duties.

leadership.evidence: Should promote and support these principles by leadership and example (Seven Principles appendix).

coc.note: Members must ensure their conduct accords with the Seven Principles of Public Life, defined in an annex to the Code.

selflessness.evidence: Listed and defined in the Code's Seven Principles of Public Life annex.

integrity.evidence: Ofcom must maintain a reputation for impartiality, integrity and high professional standards; Seven Principles annex.

objectivity.evidence: Members must not bring Ofcom's impartiality and objectivity into question; Seven Principles annex.

accountability.evidence: Listed and defined in the Code's Seven Principles annex.

openness.evidence: Listed and defined in the Code's Seven Principles annex.

honesty.evidence: Listed and defined in the Code's Seven Principles annex.

leadership.evidence: Listed and defined in the Code's Seven Principles annex.

orgs.name: Guy's & St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust

classification.basis: NHS foundation trust, statutory public function

coc.note: Governors' Code requires members to 'uphold the Nolan principles of public life'; the constitution enumerates all seven.

selflessness.evidence: Uphold the Nolan principles of public life; Selflessness enumerated: take decisions solely in terms of the public interest.

integrity.evidence: Enumerated in the Trust constitution's Seven Principles of Public Life.

objectivity.evidence: Enumerated in the Trust constitution's Seven Principles of Public Life.

accountability.evidence: Enumerated in the Trust constitution's Seven Principles of Public Life.

openness.evidence: Enumerated in the Trust constitution's Seven Principles of Public Life.

honesty.evidence: Enumerated in the Trust constitution's Seven Principles of Public Life.

leadership.evidence: Enumerated in the Trust constitution's Seven Principles of Public Life.

classification.basis: Central government, Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010

coc.note: Uses four own values (integrity, honesty, objectivity, impartiality); does not name the Seven Principles, but substantively covers most.

selflessness.evidence: You must not misuse your official position... to further your private interests; must not be influenced by the prospect of personal gain.

integrity.evidence: Named core value; must not accept gifts or hospitality which might reasonably be seen to compromise your integrity.

objectivity.evidence: Named core value; provide advice on the basis of the evidence; take decisions on the merits of the case.

accountability.evidence: Civil servants are accountable to ministers, who in turn are accountable to Parliament; keep accurate official records.

openness.evidence: Handle information as openly as possible within the legal framework (qualified, sits against a non-disclosure duty).

honesty.evidence: Named core value; set out the facts truthfully and correct any errors; must not deceive or knowingly mislead.

leadership.evidence: No leadership-by-example provision in the Nolan sense.

coc.note: Structured around four themes, not the Seven Principles; substantively covers most.

selflessness.evidence: Prioritise people: you put the interests of people using or needing nursing or midwifery services first.

integrity.evidence: Promote professionalism and trust; act with honesty and integrity, upholding the reputation of your profession.

objectivity.evidence: Always practise in line with the best available evidence; make sure any advice given is evidence-based.

accountability.evidence: The professions we regulate exercise professional judgement and are accountable for their work.

openness.evidence: Be open and candid with all service users about all aspects of care, including when mistakes or harm have taken place.

honesty.evidence: Provide honest, accurate and constructive feedback; be open and honest when something goes wrong.

leadership.evidence: Uphold the reputation of your profession at all times (professional leadership, not the Nolan championing-by-example sense).

coc.doc_type: Standards of Professional Behaviour (Police Conduct Regs)
coc.note: The statutory Standards of Professional Behaviour focus on conduct; the College of Policing Code of Ethics separately states its principles are based on the Seven Principles of Public Life.

selflessness.evidence: Officers do not abuse their powers or authority and do not compromise or abuse their position (anti-self-interest, not a full public-interest duty).

integrity.evidence: Honesty and Integrity: officers are honest, act with integrity and do not compromise or abuse their position.

objectivity.evidence: Only give and carry out lawful orders; use force only where necessary, proportionate and reasonable (no explicit merit/evidence standard).

accountability.evidence: Report, challenge or take action against colleagues' conduct that falls below the Standards; report any action taken against them.

openness.evidence: No openness provision; the Confidentiality standard restricts disclosure to the proper course of police duties.

honesty.evidence: Honesty and Integrity: officers are honest and do not compromise their position.

leadership.evidence: Challenging and Reporting Improper Conduct implies leading by example, but no explicit leadership duty.

classification.basis: Academy trust: public education function, private (charitable company) legal form
